title: Find All Duplicates in an Array
statement:
You are given an integer array `nums` of length `n`. Every value in it lies between `1` and `n` inclusive, and no value occurs more than twice. Return the values that occur exactly twice, in any order (an empty list when there are none).

Your algorithm should run in O(n) time and use only constant extra space, not counting the list you return.
constraints: Each value in nums appears once or twice
notes:
## Intuition

A hash set of seen values solves this in O(n) time but O(n) extra space. The constraint `1 <= nums[i] <= n` means every value names a valid index: value `v` belongs to slot `v - 1`. The sign of that slot can serve as a "seen" flag. Flip it negative the first time `v` shows up; if it is already negative, `v` has been seen before, so it is a duplicate. The magnitudes stay intact, so each slot still tells us its own value.

## Approach

1. Walk through `nums` with index `i`. Take `value = Math.abs(nums[i])`, since an earlier step may have flipped this slot.
2. Let `index = value - 1` be the slot that tracks `value`.
3. If `nums[index]` is already negative, `value` was seen before: add it to `result`.
4. Otherwise negate `nums[index]` to record the first sighting.
5. Return `result`.

## Example 1, step by step

`nums = [4,3,2,7,8,2,3,1]`. Values `4, 3, 2, 7, 8` flip slots `3, 2, 1, 6, 7`, giving `[4,-3,-2,-7,8,2,-3,-1]`. At `i = 5`, `value = 2` and slot `1` holds `-3`, already negative, so `2` is pushed. At `i = 6`, `value = |-3| = 3` and slot `2` holds `-2`, so `3` is pushed. At `i = 7`, `value = |-1| = 1` flips slot `0`. The result is `[2, 3]`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n): one pass with constant work per element.
- Space: O(1) besides the output; the flags live in the signs of `nums`.

## Pitfalls

- Read `Math.abs(nums[i])`: the current slot may already have been negated by an earlier value.
- Index with `value - 1`; values start at `1`, so `nums[value]` runs past the end for `value = n`.
- Each value appears at most twice, so a value is pushed at most once; with three copies this trick would report it twice.
- The method changes `nums`; restore the signs afterwards if the caller still needs the array.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `i` | position being read |
| `value` | the true value at `i`, sign removed |
| `index` | the slot whose sign records whether `value` was seen |
| `result` | values found twice |

narration.2: Collect the values found twice here.
narration.4: Strip the sign: an earlier value may have flipped this slot, but its magnitude is still the original value.
narration.5: Value v is tracked by slot v - 1, which always exists because 1 <= v <= n.
narration.6: A negative slot means this value was already seen once.
narration.7: So this is its second copy: record it.
narration.9: First sighting: flip the slot negative to remember it.
narration.12: Every value seen twice has been recorded exactly once.
